items.title: Africa: Mounting Fatalities Linked to Militant Islamist Violence in Africa Amid Shifting Tactics
items.description: [ACSS] Fatalities linked to militant Islamist violence in Africa surpassed 20,000 deaths for the fourth consecutive year, underscoring the resiliency of militant groups across the Sahel, Somalia, the Lake Chad Basin, and Mozambique.

items.title: Somalia and Italy Together for Fisheries and the Blue Economy
items.description: (ANSA) - NAIROBI, 12 AGO - The Italian Ambassador to Somalia, Pier Mario Daccò Coppi, met with the Minister of Fisheries and the Blue Economy, Ahmed Hassan Adan, to receive an update on ongoing programs and exchange views on the prospects for a greater Italian presence in the sector. The Somali minister thanked Italy for funding the cooperation project aimed at strengthening the fisheries supply chain in the city of Bosaso (Puntland), expressing the hope that this initiative could be replicated in other locations across Somalia to contribute to the development of coastal communities. Minister
items.titleIt: Somalia and Italy Together for Fisheries and the Blue Economy

items.title: EU to Support Libya in the Fight Against Terrorism and for Border Security
items.description: (ANSA) - IL CAIRO, 07 AGO - The European Union’s ambassador to Libya, Nicola Orlando, met yesterday in Tripoli with members of the 3+3 Joint Military Committee, which brings together representatives from Tripoli and Benghazi under the auspices of the Ministry of Defense and the General Command of the Libyan Arab Armed Forces. items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.
items.titleIt: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab

items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.title: Central African Republic: UAE's Global South Utilities Inaugurates 50mw Solar Plant in Central African Republic
items.description: [Horn Diplomat] Bangui (Horndiplomat) -- Abu Dhabi-based Global South Utilities (GSU) has inaugurated a 50-megawatt solar power plant in the Central African Republic, a project the company says is the largest infrastructure development in the country's history and will increase national electricity generation capacity by more than 60%.
items.titleIt: Central African Republic: UAE's Global South Utilities Inaugurates 50mw Solar Plant in Central African Republic

items.title: Sudan: Sudan Paramilitary Forces Attack Border Town, Army Alleges Assault Launched From Ethiopia
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) attacked the border town of Geissan in Blue Nile State on Tuesday, according to the RSF and local authorities, while a Sudanese army source told AFP that the assault was launched "from inside Ethiopian territory."
items.titleIt: Sudan: Sudan Paramilitary Forces Attack Border Town, Army Alleges Assault Launched From Ethiopia

items.title: Malawi: Diplomatic Tension Erupts As SA Tells Malawi to Reimburse Deportation Costs
items.description: [Nyasa Times] South Africa has sparked a diplomatic storm after formally demanding that Malawi, Nigeria and Ethiopia reimburse part of the R292 million (about K29 billion) it has spent this year deporting undocumented migrants -- with Malawians making up the largest share of those removed.
items.titleIt: Malawi: Diplomatic Tension Erupts As SA Tells Malawi to Reimburse Deportation Costs

items.title: Kenya: MPs to Consider Six Bills Seeking Sweeping Reforms in Education Sector
items.description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The National Assembly is set to consider six Bills proposing far-reaching reforms across Kenya's education sector, with the proposed legislation targeting basic education governance, national assessments, curriculum development, teacher training, tertiary education funding and the recognition of academic and professional qualifications.
items.titleIt: Kenya: MPs to Consider Six Bills Seeking Sweeping Reforms in Education Sector

items.title: Tigray rebels accuse Ethiopia of drone strikes amid fears of renewed war
items.description: Tigray rebel authorities have accused Ethiopia’s federal government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in the region, raising fears of a renewed conflict nearly four years after a peace deal ended a devastating two-year war.
items.titleIt: Tigray rebels accuse Ethiopia of drone strikes amid fears of renewed war

items.title: Ambassador Del Monaco Meets with the Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya
items.description: (ANSA) - ROMA, 07 AGO - The Italian Ambassador to the Republic of Kenya and the Seychelles, Vincenzo Del Monaco, met with the Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya, Kamau Thugge, with whom he had “an important exchange of information.” “It was an opportunity to discuss the country’s economic situation,” the embassy noted, “and the growing bilateral relationship between Italy and Kenya.” Read article...

items.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopians Make Up Overwhelming Majority of Migrants Arriving in Yemen Amid Worsening Regional Conditions
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopian nationals accounted for 91% of the 13,687 migrants who arrived in Yemen in July 2026, making them by far the largest group of migrants recorded entering the conflict-affected country during the month, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
